trust_decision.summary: MoQSession decides whether a peer-owned proxygen StreamReadHandle* is still live (not yet invalidated by a FIN, a read exception or stream cancellation) before calling getID/getCancelToken/readStreamData/stopSending on it; at the pinned commit liveness is tracked ad hoc per coroutine with raw pointers, and is lost when a FIN read in one coroutine is handed to another coroutine (or buffered) together with the raw handle.

landing_point.why: The summary names MoQSession::dataStreamReadLoop and 'keeps using a stream read handle after reading a FIN'; an engineer starts there, at the FIN handling at moxygen/MoQSession.cpp:4222-4224 and the stopSendingGuard at moxygen/MoQSession.cpp:4032-4039.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report names dataStreamReadLoop, and controlReadLoop already nulls the handle on FIN (moxygen/MoQSession.cpp:3403-3405) and on exception (moxygen/MoQSession.cpp:3387-3388), so a solver can argue the control path and the bidi/pre-setup demuxers already respect the FIN contract; the handoff-with-FIN case only arises when a peer packs the first frame and the FIN into one write, which looks like a niche uni-control/draft-18 corner.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Buffered bytes that arrived together with the FIN must still be parsed and delivered (object with finSubgroup, SETUP parsed, SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS answered), the FIN must still drive controlReadLoop close handling (firePeerTermination/failPendingRequestOnEarlyClose/writeFin, gated on fin), and STOP_SENDING must still be sent with control->readCancelCode() or the fetch cancel code when a live stream is abandoned early; a fix that drops initialData, skips the handoff, or stops sending STOP_SENDING altogether breaks these.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: handleClientSetup's client-direction rejection is already such a path; rejection branches are routinely added per draft.
